judged_text: The decrypted keys object is persisted as credential.key without being validated against the target app's credential schema (e.g. googleCredentialSchema) before the 200 is returned. A parent-app bug that pushes a key missing refresh_token or access_token bricks the user's integration at the next service construction (the schema parse throws) while the webhook returns 200 'Credentials updated', so the parent app never learns it shipped a broken credential.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` and then persisted directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })` / `create({ data: { key: keys, ... } })` without any validation against an app-specific credential schema. Since other codepaths (e.g. Google/Zoom/Office365 services) rely on schema parsing of `credential.key` (e.g. `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` / `parseRefreshTokenResponse(..., schema)`), storing malformed keys can break downstream integration usage while the webhook still returns HTTP 200, matching the finding’s described failure mode.
